title.narrative: UNICEF WASH Strengthening Community Resilience to COVID-19 and Climate Shocks
UNICEF WASH Stärkt motståndskraft mot Covid-19 och klimatchocker

description.narrative: 15 000 000 SEK bidrag till UNICEFs intervention, via Vatten, Sanitet och Hygien-sektorn, till åtgärder mot COVID-19 i Kenya 2019/2020, i gränssnittet mellan humanitärt och och långsiktigt utvecklingsarbete; Vattenförsörjning för att förebygga och kontrollera smitta, sanitet och hygien, informationsarbete för nya hygien-normer, samt förbättrad samordning av externt stöd till Kenya inom vatten, sanitet och hygien under COVID-19-krisen. En del av insatsen kommer att genomföras av UNICEF själva, andra genomföras av tredje part, dels genom upphandling, dels genom vidareförmedling. Insatsen är en påbyggnad på redan pågående UNICEF-program, med inarbetade rutiner, och risken i genomförandet anses genomgående låg. För sanitets- och hygien komponenten har den lokala organisationen Sanergy redan identifierats genom ansökningsförfarande.

UNICEF component of 15 000 000 SEK Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sector response to COVID-19 in Kenya 2019/2020, in the HUM/ development nexus; Water supply to prevent and control infection, Sanitation & Hygiene, community sensitation for new social norms for hygiene behaviour, and support to improved coordination of external support to Kenya in WASH during the COVID-19 crisis.
Part of the programme will be implemented by UNICEF themselves, others will be implemented by third parties. either through procurement, or through forwarding of funds. The programme is an add-on to already existing UNICEF initiatives in the sector, with existing routines, and the implementation risk is generally seen as low. For the Sanitation & Hygiene Component, the local organisation Sanergy has already been identified through application procedure.

The overall objective is to strengthen community resilience to Covid-19 in informal settlements of Nairobi County and climate shocks in drought prone Samburu County through improved access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services. The objectives are to increase access to sustainable WASH services in informal settlements of Nairobi County and to increase access to climate resilient and sustainable water services in water insecure Samburu County.
Outcome 1. 170,000 people gain access to WASH services in informal settlements of Nairobi County
Outcome 2. 45,000 people have access to climate resilient and sustained WASH services and community climate resilience is strengthened in Samburu County

sector.narrative: Basic drinking water supply and basic sanitation

description.narrative:
Outcome 1. 170,000 people gain access to WASH services in informal settlements of Nairobi County The program has increased availability of WASH services in Nairobi informal settlements, the results already show that 37,500 out of targeted 20,000 people (187.5%) were provided with access to safe drinking water in communities and health care facilities. UNICEF has provided daily access to safely managed sanitation to 180,364 people (against a target of 170,000 people) in the two Nairobi informal settlements (Mukuru and Mathare) through a network of 5,491 active container based toilets in partnership with Sanergy (Freshlife). During the reporting period, the total number of people served increased by 37,280 (32.9%) by manufacturing and installing or operating 808 more container based toilets. The network of these low cost toilets has contributed to improving human health and well being and the surrounding natural environment. The full sanitation value chain is being addressed. The waste collection service safely removes 2,139 metric tons of waste monthly from these toilets which is converted to energy, fertilizer, and insect protein for animal feed.
Building on the successful collaboration with Huru International Kenya in phase I of the project this was continued in phase II and so far 5,730 girls have received reusable Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) kits. As a result, girls dignity and self esteem has been upheld and they are able to attend school contributing to improvement of their academic performance. Huru International Kenya is also implementing community sensitization activities on Covid-19 prevention and MHM in informal settlements of Nairobi and 120,000 community members (against a target of 120,000 people) have been reached and sensitized on this important topic. As a result, the community members have increased awareness on Covid-19 prevention practices especially hand washing with water and soap. This has also contributed to reduction of water related diseases due to improved hygiene practices at the community and household level.
Outcome 2. 45,000 people have access to climate resilient and sustained WASH services and community climate resilience is strengthened in Samburu County
The County Water Services department identified a total of three villages with potential for ground water harvesting structures. The sites are located across the two sub counties of Samburu East and Samburu North Sub Counties. Three sand dams have been constructed. For rehabilitation of 8 boreholes, UNICEF has established a partnership with FCA. Community consultation and sensitization has been done for the identified sites to ensure ownership of the projects during the rehabilitation. 18,000 out of targeted 19,000 people (95%) people were provided access to sustainable and climate resilient water supply supplies, the rest will be finalized during the extended activity period. UNICEF conducted a series of consultative meetings with the National and County MoH to set a target and identify geographical locations to deliver 150 villages to Open Defecation Free (ODF)certified status, targeting 45,000 people living in safe and clean environment in Samburu. 58 villages have been triggered and following up is ongoing to verify ODF. A total of 114 Community Health Volunteers have been trained on the resilience of sanitation services. As a result, awareness has been created on appropriate sanitation and hygiene practices and has contributed to improved health of the community members. All targeted 45,000 (100%) people have been provided access to climate resilient sanitation and hygiene services in communities and schools in Samburu County.
Through the Zuhura Impact partnership, a Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship Challenge for young social innovators, aged between 18 and 24 years, with a particular focus on young women and youth from Samburu County has been designed. The challenge invited young change makers who are passionate about addressing the Climate Change crisis affecting their communities/country. 75 young people in Samburu participated in the entrepreneurship boot camp
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
